target.title: fix(mattermost): cap opaque, outbound, and monitor resource caches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded in-process Maps across three Mattermost runtime surfaces:

| Surface | Maps | Pre-fix behavior |
|---------|------|------------------|
| **Monitor** (`monitor-resources.ts`) | per-monitor `channelCache`, `userCache` | TTL-based reuse but **no size cap** |
| **Outbound send** (`send.ts`) | `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` | Grew with every distinct `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple |
| **Opaque target resolution** (`target-resolution.ts`) | `mattermostOpaqueTargetCache` | 26-char ID lookups cached forever |

**Concrete example:** A busy Mattermost gateway monitoring 2 000 channels and resolving 3 000 opaque user IDs retains thousands of monitor + opaque cache entries indefinitely, plus unbounded outbound resolution caches under multi-recipient routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Centralizes cache writes through helpers that call `pruneMapToMaxSize` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` immediately after each `.set`:

| Cache | Cap | File |
|-------|-----|------|
| Monitor `channelCache` | **1000** | `monitor-resources.ts` |
| Monitor `userCache` | **1000** | `monitor-resources.ts` |
| Outbound `botUserCache` | **256** | `send.ts` via `cacheOutboundEntry` |
| Outbound `userByNameCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Outbound `channelByNameCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Outbound `dmChannelCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Opaque `mattermostOpaqueTargetCache` | **1024** | `target-resolution.ts` |

TTL semantics for monitor caches are unchanged; eviction only bounds maximum retained entries.

## User Impact

**Before:** Mattermost-connected gateways accumulate unbounded in-process cache memory on long uptimes.

**After:** Each cache is capped; oldest insertion-order entries evict once limits are exceeded. Evicted entries behave like a cache miss (re-fetch / re-resolve on next use).

## Evidence

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-resources.ts:47–48,95–110` — monitor cache caps + `setCachedValue` prune
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:71–86` — outbound caps + shared `cacheOutboundEntry`
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/target-resolution.ts:19–25` — opaque target cap + `cacheMattermostOpaqueTarget`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` implementation
- Diff: +123/−12 across five files; regressions in `monitor-resources.test.ts` and `target-resolution.test.ts`

### Behavior proof

#### 1) Node runtime (production constants + helper shapes, no Vitest)

```text
=== Mattermost process cache cap proof (production constants + helpers, no Vitest) ===
Node: v22.22.0

[monitor channelCache]
  after 1001 resolveChannelInfo writes → size 1000 (cap 1000)
  chan-0 evicted: true
  chan-1000 retained: true

[opaque target cache]
  after 1025 resolveMattermostOpaqueTarget writes → size 1024 (cap 1024)
  first opaque id evicted: true

[outbound dmChannelCache via cacheOutboundEntry]
  after 1025 DM resolves → size 1024 (cap 1024)
  oldest DM evicted: true
  newest DM retained: true

[outbound cap table wired in send.ts]
  botUserCache: 256
  userByNameCache: 1024
  channelByNameCache: 1024
  dmChannelCache: 1024
```

#### 2) Monitor channel cache — call-site regression

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-resources.test.ts -t "evicts oldest channel" --reporter=verbose

 ✓ mattermost monitor resources > evicts oldest channel cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 5ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 7 skipped (8)
   Duration  3.59s
```

Regression flow (`createMattermostMonitorResources` → `resolveChannelInfo`):

1. Resolve `chan-0` → `fetchMattermostChannel` **1×**
2. Resolve `chan-1` … `chan-1000` → **1000** more API calls (**1001** total)
3. Re-resolve `chan-0` → `fetchMattermostChannel` **1×** again (oldest monitor channel entry evicted)

#### 3) Opaque target cache — call-site regression

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/target-resolution.test.ts -t "evicts oldest opaque" --reporter=verbose

 ✓ mattermost target resolution > evicts oldest opaque target cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 4ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 4 skipped (5)
```

Regression flow (`resolveMattermostOpaqueTarget`):

1. Resolve first 26-char id (`a…a`) → `fetchMattermostUser` **1×**
2. Resolve **1024** additional opaque ids → **1025** total user lookups
3. Re-resolve first id → `fetchMattermostUser` **1×** again (oldest opaque cache entry evicted)

#### 4) Full touched test files still green

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-resources.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/target-resolution.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
```

Outbound send caches are wired through `cacheOutboundEntry` + `pruneMapToMaxSize` in `send.ts` (Node proof above demonstrates DM cache eviction contract). Dedicated outbound eviction regressions live on [#101800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101800); this PR adds monitor + opaque caps and outbound wiring in the same helper pattern.

**Proof gap:** No redacted live Mattermost server logs in this validation environment. Node reproduction + monitor/opaque regressions cover the production cache helpers; optional supplemental proof is a gateway log under sustained distinct-channel/opaque-id traffic showing stable cache size.
